summary: Verified GT double-deduction bug fix. Backend: 3/3 pytest tests pass in test_gt_single_deduction.py. (1) POST /api/calculations/run {recalculate:true} -> processed=42550, fully_mapped_count=41977 (exact expected). (2) Full paginated invariant audit over ALL 41,977 mapped rows (27,942 sales + ~14k return): round(expected_settlement + total_deductions, 2) == round(base_nsv, 2) with ZERO violations. Proves GT (and every component) is deducted exactly once against raw NSV. (3) Direct compute_expected() call with client masters (NSV 348, commission 4%, fixed fee 37 + 18% GST, GT 59, return fee 106, tcs 0.5%, tds 0.1%) returns total_deductions=-12.03 and expected_settlement=-335.97, EXACTLY as required by spec (was -276.97). Frontend: login admin@fundle.ai/admin123 OK; Calculations page loads, drawer opens on row click and renders the 'Expected Charges & Deductions' list plus 'Total Deductions' and 'Expected Settlement' rows. Spot-checked drawer: order 100133986504 sale Jackets NSV 4424 -> Total Deductions 846.50, Expected Settlement 3577.50, invariant 4424 - 846.50 = 3577.50 holds. Spot-checked 3 return rows via API: all satisfy es+td == -|nsv|. No 'kazo'/'KAZO' in DOM. Regression clean.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix in /app/backend/routers/calculations.py compute_expected is clean: 'return' branch uses expected_settlement = signed_nsv - total_deductions (line 353), 'sales' branch uses eff_nsv - total_deductions (line 375). nsv_after_gt is retained only as the commission/TCS/TDS base — correct.
The pre-existing minor Sub-Category-filter stale-response race noted in iteration_3 is unchanged (not part of this bug scope).

Known/expected and NOT reported: 573 unmapped calculations, reconciliation 0-matched, AI health grade F. rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: compute_expected() for the 'return' branch summed GT into total_deductions AND used nsv_after_gt (which had already subtracted GT) as the base for expected_settlement = nsv_after_gt - total_deductions, so GT was deducted twice. Fix: switch the settlement anchor to the raw signed NSV — 'return' uses expected_settlement = signed_nsv - total_deductions, 'sales' uses eff_nsv - total_deductions. nsv_after_gt is retained only as the base for commission/TCS/TDS. Verified by asserting the identity expected_settlement + total_deductions == base_nsv across 41,977 mapped calculations (0 violations).
